summary.title: Gluon Radiation of an Expanding Color Skyrmion in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
summary.executive_summary: This paper calculates the density of states and energy spectrum of gluon radiation emitted by an expanding color skyrmion within the quark-gluon plasma (QGP). Using a semiclassical approach applied to a nonlinear sigma model describing an ideal fluid, the author derives the nonabelian current for a time-dependent soliton solution. The study compares these results with existing literature on jet quenching and medium-induced radiation. The findings reveal a specific spectral pattern: a fast fall-off in the ultraviolet (UV) region, a smooth peak dominating the intermediate energy range, and a long tail in the infrared (IR). The IR behavior is characterized by a number density scaling as 1/sqrt(k), which differs from the 1/k scaling found in models assuming an infinitely large medium. The work suggests that the finite size of the soliton (R0) softens the IR behavior compared to infinite-medium approximations. Additionally, the study highlights a hierarchy between the characteristic momentum of the skyrmion (1/R0) and the typical frequency of medium-induced radiation (omega_C), implying distinct physical mechanisms at play. The results are presented as functions of a dimensionless parameter lambda, with numerical results provided for lambda values of 1/15, 2/15, and 1/5.

The medium-induced radiation frequency omega_C is significantly larger than the characteristic momentum 1/R0 of the skyrmion.
The hydrodynamical approach can intrinsically address the eccentricity of elliptic flow via nonabelian color currents.

Research Context
The study addresses gluon radiation in the hydrodynamic stage of QGP evolution. Medium induced radiation is typically explored in the context of jet quenching. Prior work often models the medium as a collection of colored static scattering centers. Existing literature on jet quenching often assumes an infinitely large medium size. This assumption leads to an asymptotic number density scaling of 1/k in small k. However, the expanding nature of the RHIC fireball requires a different model. A recent discovery of single skyrmion solutions in color fluid provides a new framework. These solutions describe a time-dependent skyrmion that expands in time. This expansion aligns with the physical nature of the fireball generated in RHIC. The pattern of gluon radiation from these non-static configurations remains unexplored.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is the calculation of the gluon radiation spectrum from an expanding color skyrmion. The study hypothesizes a fast fall-off in the UV side of the spectrum. A smooth peak is predicted to dominate the intermediate energy range. A long tail is expected to be the characteristic feature in the IR. The characteristic momentum 1/R0 is hypothesized to be smaller than the medium-induced frequency. The approach aims to address the eccentricity of elliptic flow via nonabelian color currents.
